messages.subject: looking for Cmatrix in generic0
parts:
Hi

Still playing around with INLA, I encountered some odd behaviour concerning the "generic0" model.
If I use a function (inlaFUN), in which I call inla( f(..,model="generic0", Cmatrix=Q),...)
then Q is not found by inla() if it is only defined in inlaFUN().

Here an example:

# generic0 example from http://www.r-inla.org/models/latent-models
library(INLA)
n=100
z=1:n
y=sin(z/n*2*pi)+rnorm(n,mean=0,sd=0.5)
data=data.frame(y=y,z=z)
Q = toeplitz(c(2,-1, rep(0,n-3),-1))
Q[1,1] = Q[n,n] = 1
Q[n,1] = Q[1,n] = 0
## Q as dense
formula1 = y ~ f(z, model="generic0", Cmatrix = Q,
rankdef=1, constr=TRUE, diagonal=1e-05)
result1 = inla(formula1, data=data, family="gaussian")


# Define some wrapper-function inlaFUN(...) calling inla(...):
inlaFUN <- function(Qr){
Q <- Qr
result1 = inla(formula1, data=data, family="gaussian")
return(result1)
}

#It works if Q is defined:
Qr <- Q
result1F <- inlaFUN(Qr)
#But removing Q from the environment and relying on Q <- Qr within inlaFUN(...)
# will cause an error as inla(...) does not find Q:
rm(Q)
result1F <- inlaFUN(Qr)

This is somewhat unexpected as for other arguments to f(...) e.g. for settings concerning
hyperparameters (hyper = list(theta = list(prior = ..) this usually works.
I guess it has something to do with the environment in which inla(..) is looking for Q
but for me this behaviour is different than for other parameters.

Is this thus a model="generic0" specific problem?
Or is it a misapplication from my side?

Thanks for your support!
Regards,

Rafael

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] looking for Cmatrix in generic0
parts:
R is often very confusing when it comes to locating variables...

In this case, try supplying it in the data parameter, as
  data=c(as.list(data), list(Q=Q))
so that inla has more direct access to it.

This is what we do with e.g. Spde objects that are also used as f() function parameters.

Finn
